newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs likely to approve tank sale to Algeria - PM.
newsitem.headline: Czechs likely to approve tank sale to Algeria - PM.

text.p: The Czech cabinet will probably approve the proposed sale of about 100 surplus Soviet-made T-72 tanks to the Algerian government, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Wednesday.

Speaking at a news conference, Klaus said a government meeting on Wednesday evening was likely to approve the deal, which would provide the Czech army with funds to buy 12 new Czech-made light subsonic Aero L-39 fighter aircraft.
"The cabinet is prepared to decide on this in a positive way," Klaus told reporters.

He did not give any more details of the proposed transaction with Algeria, racked by a bitter conflict between the government and Islamist guerrillas. Czech media have said the price for the used un-modernised tanks would be around 1.3 billion crowns ($41 million).
"From the point of view of the foreign policy interests of the Czech Republic there are no objections," Foreign Affairs Minister Josef Zieleniec told the news conference.
The former Czechoslovakia was once one of the world's largest arms producers, but curtailed arms exports after the 1989 fall of Communism.
After the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993, the Czech government approved an arms export licencing procedure which set up strict cabinet oversight.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria since 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a lead.
The authorities barred radical Islamists from this month's election but allowed two moderate Islamist parties to compete. These won a total of 103 seats in the 380-member National Assembly.
